{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that cleanliness priming would lead to less severe moral judgments than neutral priming among participants exerting low response effort, but that this effect would be absent or reversed among participants exerting high response effort.",
  "design": "mixed, with priming condition (cleanliness vs. neutral) as a between-subjects factor and response effort (low vs. high) as a between-subjects factor.",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Participants were randomly assigned to complete a sentence unscrambling task using either cleanliness-related words or neutral words. Response effort was manipulated by instructions: the low effort group was told to work as quickly as possible without worrying about accuracy, while the high effort group was told to perform to the best of their ability.",
  "outcome_measure": "Moral judgment ratings on six vignettes (e.g., dog, trolley, wallet, plane, résumé, kitten) on a 10-point scale, averaged into a composite score.",
  "population_and_setting": "English-speaking adults residing in the United States recruited via Amazon Mechanical Turk.",
  "sample_size_total": 440,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited from Amazon Mechanical Turk in exchange for $0.50 compensation.",
  "analysis_plan": "A 2 (priming condition) x 2 (response effort) factorial ANOVA to test for an interaction effect, followed by simple effects tests.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants were excluded if they guessed the study hypothesis or if they exhibited rapid insufficient effort responding (IER) on the moral judgment tasks, defined as responding faster than 675 words per minute on two or more vignettes."
}
